lesson.title: Asking and Pointing
lesson.subtitle: Question Words, This and That
lesson.description: Ask who, what, where and how, and identify people and objects as here or there.

learning_objectives: Choose a demonstrative expression for singular or plural things.

overview.topic_description: Ask who, what, where and how, and identify people and objects as here or there.

examples.teaching_note: 多少钱 is the routine shopping question for a price.

examples.english: How many students are in this class?

items.pos_note: Interrogative pronoun asking how many or how much (多少钱、多少人). It is not itself a classifier and can directly precede a noun.

examples.teaching_note: 哪 selects one among known choices; 本 is the measure word for books.

examples.hanzi: 老师问：“你们想读哪本书？”
examples.pinyin: lǎoshī wèn: “nǐmen xiǎng dú nǎ běn shū?”
examples.english: The teacher asked, “Which book would you like to read?”
examples.teaching_note: The question word comes before the book classifier.
哪个 asks which one; 个 stands for the classifier of the implied object.
哪里 asks where an institution or object is located.

examples.english: "Excuse me, where is the bookstore?" she asked.
examples.teaching_note: Written dialogue: 哪里 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
哪儿 means where, with the 儿 pronunciation typical of northern Mandarin.
Written dialogue: 哪儿 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.
哪些 means which ones when choosing several items.
那 points to something away from the speaker, in contrast to 这.

items.pos_note: Demonstrative pronoun; can also have discourse-connecting uses.

examples.teaching_note: 那边 denotes a place over there, away from the speaker.

examples.english: There is a restaurant over there.

examples.teaching_note: 那个 identifies a particular item; 个 is its classifier.
那里 means “there” and is a full location word.
那儿 is a northern-style alternative to 那里 for “there.”

examples.pinyin: “qǐng zài nàr děng lǎoshī.” tā shuō.
examples.english: “Please wait for the teacher over there,” she said.
examples.teaching_note: The quoted speaker uses the erhua form for “there.”
那些 points to several items away from the speaker.

examples.pinyin: nàxiē xuéshēng dōu zài jiàoshì lǐ.
examples.english: Those students are all in the classroom.

examples.teaching_note: 谁 asks for a person’s identity; shéi is used here, while shuí is an accepted alternative.

examples.pinyin: “zhè shì shéi de shū?” lǎoshī wèn.
examples.english: "Whose book is this?" the teacher asked.
examples.teaching_note: Written dialogue: 谁 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.

examples.english: What do you want to eat?
examples.teaching_note: 什么 asks what food the listener wants; it is a general interrogative pronoun.

examples.english: "What do you want to drink?" she asked.
examples.teaching_note: Written dialogue: 什么 is used naturally in a spoken exchange, rather than forced into formal prose.

examples.english: How do you write this character?
examples.teaching_note: 怎么写 asks how to write a particular Chinese character.

examples.english: How do you do this question?

items.pos_note: Interrogative pro-form meaning how, often adverbial in sentences.

examples.teaching_note: 你觉得怎么样 asks for someone’s impression or opinion.

examples.pinyin: “zhè jiā fàndiàn de cài zěnmeyàng?” tā wèn.
examples.english: “How’s the food at this restaurant?” he asked.
examples.teaching_note: The question word asks for an evaluation in quoted speech.

items.pos_note: Interrogative pro-form meaning how/how about; often adverbial in sentences.

examples.teaching_note: 这 means this; 这是什么 is a standard way to ask what something is.

examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū shì xīn de.

examples.teaching_note: 请到这边来 invites someone to come over to this side.

examples.hanzi: 学校在这边，医院在那边。
examples.pinyin: xuéxiào zài zhèbiān, yīyuàn zài nàbiān.
examples.english: The school is on this side, and the hospital is over there.

examples.teaching_note: 这个 means “this one,” with the noun inferred from context.
这里 is a full location word meaning “here.”

examples.hanzi: 这里可以喝茶，也可以看书。
examples.pinyin: zhèlǐ kěyǐ hē chá, yě kěyǐ kàn shū.
examples.english: You can drink tea and read books here.

examples.teaching_note: 这儿 is a northern-style spoken alternative to 这里.

examples.pinyin: “zhèr yǒu yì jiā shūdiàn.” tā shuō.
examples.teaching_note: The quoted speaker uses the erhua form for “here.”
这些 means these plural items, here the apples.

examples.pinyin: zhèxiē xuéshēng dōu zài xué Hànyǔ.
examples.english: These students are all learning Chinese.

grammar_points.title: Asking what
grammar_points.explanation: Question words generally stay in the position of the information being requested.

grammar_points.title: Pointing nearby
grammar_points.explanation: Demonstratives identify nearby or distant people, objects and places.

questions.explanation: The correct vocabulary entry means “how many; how much”.

questions.prompt: In the example “这个多少钱？” (zhège duōshao qián?), what is happening?
questions.explanation: Use the complete sentence meaning as your guide.

questions.prompt: Write this in Mandarin: “How many students are in this class?”
questions.answer: 这个班有多少学生？ (zhège bān yǒu duōshao xuéshēng?)
questions.explanation: Compare your answer with the example and its tone-marked pinyin.

questions.prompt: Reading comprehension: What is Xiao Li shopping for?
questions.explanation: Check against the connected reading passage, not the vocabulary cards.

questions.prompt: Reading comprehension: Which phone is cheaper?
questions.explanation: Check against the connected reading passage, not the vocabulary cards.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud: Ask where the school is.
questions.answer: 这个学校在哪里？ (Zhège xuéxiào zài nǎlǐ?) — Where is this school?
questions.explanation: Illustrative answer. Other natural responses may be correct.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud: Ask which book someone wants.
questions.answer: 你要哪本书？ (Nǐ yào nǎ běn shū?) — Which book do you want?
questions.explanation: Illustrative answer. Other natural responses may be correct.

dialogue.title: Asking and Pointing
dialogue.context_en: At a bookstore, one friend asks which object and where; the other uses near/far demonstratives.

patterns.title: This versus that
patterns.explanation_en: 这 (zhè) points to something closer in the discourse or situation; 那 (nà) points to something more distant. Add a classifier when identifying a specific item.

examples.english: That item of clothing is pretty.

patterns.pattern_hanzi: 这/那 + 量词 + 名词

patterns.title: Choose the right question word
patterns.explanation_en: 什么 (shénme) asks “what”; 谁 (shéi) asks “who”; 哪 (nǎ) asks “which”; 哪里 (nǎlǐ) asks “where”; 怎么 (zěnme) asks “how”.
patterns.pattern_hanzi: 谁 + 动词？ / 在 + 哪里？

guided_building.instruction_en: Move from a general what-question to a which-question.

model.english: What do you want to buy?

model_answer.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ běn shū?
model_answer.english: Which book do you want to buy?

model_answer.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng mǎi nǎ jiàn yīfu?
model_answer.english: Which item of clothing do you want to buy?

paragraphs.hanzi: 小李在商店里找手机。店里有很多手机。他喜欢这个，但是那个便宜一点儿。
paragraphs.pinyin: Xiǎo Lǐ zài shāngdiàn lǐ zhǎo shǒujī. Diàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō shǒujī. Tā xǐhuan zhège, dànshì nàge piányi yìdiǎnr.
paragraphs.english: Xiao Li is looking at phones in a store. There are many phones. He likes this one, but that one is a little cheaper.

questions.prompt_en: What is Xiao Li shopping for?

teaching_plan.common_pitfall: 哪 (nǎ, which) and 那 (nà, that) are different characters and tones. Do not write 那本 (nà běn) when asking “which book?”.
teaching_plan.pronunciation_focus: In spontaneous speech, 谁 has common readings shéi and shuí; avoid treating them as different words.

can_do: Choose a demonstrative expression for singular or plural things.
